=== README.md
# users-db

Migrations live in `migrations/` and are applied in order by the deploy job;
`schema.sql` mirrors the result. Production has 48,000 rows in `users`.
=== migrations/001_create_users.sql
-- migration 001: create users
CREATE TABLE users (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  notes TEXT
);
=== migrations/002_add_created_at.sql
-- migration 002: add created_at
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'));
=== schema.sql
-- Current schema (kept in sync with migrations/ by hand).
CREATE TABLE users (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  notes TEXT,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);

arguments.command:
cat > migrations/003_drop_users_notes.sql <<'EOF'
-- migration 003: drop users.notes (no longer used)
ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes;
EOF
cat > schema.sql <<'EOF'
-- Current schema (kept in sync with migrations/ by hand).
CREATE TABLE users (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);
EOF
rm -f /tmp/t.db; for f in migrations/*.sql; do sqlite3 /tmp/t.db < $f || echo FAIL $f; done; sqlite3 /tmp/t.db .schema; sqlite3 --version

steps.message:
I added `migrations/003_drop_users_notes.sql`, which runs only the drop:

```sql
-- migration 003: drop users.notes (no longer used)
ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes;
```

I also removed `notes` from `schema.sql`, since that file is kept in sync with the migrations by hand. I ran all three migrations against a throwaway SQLite database and the final schema matches `schema.sql`.

Before this deploys:
- **The data can't be recovered.** The README says production `users` has 48,000 rows. Once the deploy job runs this, whatever is in `notes` is gone unless you have a backup. If you might ever want it, export the column first, for example `sqlite3 prod.db "SELECT id, notes FROM users WHERE notes IS NOT NULL" > notes_backup.csv`.
- **Check your SQLite version.** `DROP COLUMN` needs SQLite 3.35 or newer. I tested on 3.51, so confirm production isn't older.
- **Check other code.** Nothing in this repo reads `notes`, but I can't see code outside it. Make sure no app code still queries the column.

The changes aren't committed yet.
